Timeline

22NOV 2026ProcedureGrade ACommission prepares a briefing on Cyprus

Event: 22 November 2026 · Added to monitoring: 27 November 2026

An information item on the application of Schengen rules in Cyprus has been prepared for the December Council meeting. Document ST 15799/26 was created on 22 November and received by the Austrian Parliament on 23 November. The register lists the 3–4 December meeting and the Other business section. The full text has restricted access.

Why it matters

Ministerial discussion is more likely. The presentation date and a vote on accession have not yet been confirmed.

Austrian Parliament · ST 15799/26 Council of the EU · meeting of 3 December
22NOV 2026PoliticsGrade CMedia commentary on Poland's position emerges

Event: 22 November 2026 · Added to monitoring: 23 November 2026

A Kathimerini/KNEWS columnist named Poland among countries that might be cautious in a vote. The 22 November column also mentioned Austria and the Netherlands. It supplied no official Warsaw statement or text of a reservation.

Why it matters

Poland's public statements merit monitoring. There is no basis yet to conclude that it will veto accession.

Kathimerini / KNEWS · column on Schengen readiness
20NOV 2026Technical readinessGrade A / CLarnaca and Paphos upgrade passport control

Event: 20 November 2026 · Added to monitoring: 25 November 2026

Cyprus has launched a €440,000 tender to install passport-control booths at two airports. The call was published on 20 November, with bids due by 21 December. According to Phileleftheros on 25 November, it provides for 22 booths and eight months for installation and testing after contract signature.

Why it matters

The procurement confirms airport preparations. A link between commissioning the booths and the legal accession date has not been established.

Cyprus eProcurement · MTCW/AIR2/BOOTHS/2026 Phileleftheros · airport equipment
20NOV 2026PoliticsGrade BEU and UK reaffirm commitments on the bases

Event: 20 November 2026 · Added to monitoring: 24 November 2026

At their summit, the two sides agreed to complete implementation of the protocol on the British Sovereign Base Areas in Cyprus. Point 5 of the joint statement was published on 20 November. On 10 November, the Joint Committee had reported technical progress. Specific Schengen checking arrangements at Pergamos and Strovilia have not been published.

Why it matters

The leaders' commitment supports negotiations. The accession timetable remains open.

Council of the EU · ST 16174/26, point 5 UK government · summit statement EU–UK Joint Committee · 10 November
20NOV 2026PoliticsGrade A / CEU and Türkiye discuss a Cyprus settlement

Event: 20 November 2026 · Added to monitoring: 21 November 2026

Commission Executive Vice-President Raffaele Fitto met Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan in Ankara. The Turkish Foreign Ministry confirmed the meeting. CNA and Anadolu placed different emphasis on links between a Cyprus settlement and EU–Türkiye relations.

Why it matters

This is diplomatic context. No direct link to the Council's Schengen decision has been established.

Turkish Foreign Ministry · Fidan–Fitto meeting Cyprus News Agency · Commission position Anadolu · Fidan's position
18NOV 2026PoliticsGrade BGreek Prime Minister names 1 July 2027 as a target

Event: 18 November 2026 · Added to monitoring: 20 November 2026

Kyriakos Mitsotakis linked Cyprus's accession to the start of Greece's presidency of the Council of the EU. He spoke at the intergovernmental meeting in Nicosia on 18 November. Greece will hold the presidency in the second half of 2027.

Why it matters

The July target now has public support from Athens. The Council must set the legal date.

Greek Prime Minister · Nicosia transcript
18NOV 2026ProcedureGrade AFirst December Council agenda published

Event: 18 November 2026 · Added to monitoring: 19 November 2026

Cyprus's accession is not listed separately in the provisional agenda or list of items for adoption. The documents were published on 18 November. A separate information item on Cyprus, ST 15799/26, later appeared in the register.

Why it matters

The final agenda and meeting outcomes still need to be checked.

Council of the EU · provisional agenda CM 4999/26 Council of the EU · provisional list CM 5119/26 Austrian Parliament · ST 15799/26
13NOV 2026ProcedureGrade ACommission and Cyprus presentations appear in the register

Event: 13 November 2026 · Added to monitoring: 21 November 2026

Working document WK 17427/26 concerns the Schengen evaluation at the 13 November meeting. The papers were prepared on 17 November and registered in the Austrian Parliament on 18 November. A document record marked LIMITE is available.

Why it matters

Registration shows that the working party considered the Cyprus dossier. The outcome remains unknown.

Austrian Parliament · WK 17427/26
13NOV 2026ProcedureGrade AClosure of Cyprus action plans added to working party agenda

Event: 13 November 2026

The 13 November agenda included presentation of the draft closure of action plans, discussion and possible agreement. The agenda was prepared on 11 November. The monitoring materials contain no publicly available text of an adopted decision.

Why it matters

The next significant step would be a published act closing the action plans.

Council of the EU · agenda CM 4752/1/26 REV 1 Council of the EU · working party meeting of 13 November
09NOV 2026PoliticsGrade ACommunity leaders agree on new crossings

Event: 9 November 2026

Two additional Green Line crossings were agreed under UN mediation. On 9 November, the UN named Louroujina–Lympia and Kambos–Karavostasi. The statement gave no opening dates.

Why it matters

The agreement supports intercommunal dialogue. Schengen entry and exit records remain a separate issue.

UN · statement on new crossings
27OCT 2026ProcedureGrade ADraft closure of action plans registered

Event: 27 October 2026

Draft ST 14872/26, under dossier 2026/0337 NLE, appeared in the Council register. The 27 October document concerns plans to remedy deficiencies in six areas. Access to the full draft is restricted.

Why it matters

The procedure has reached a draft decision. Adoption still requires confirmation.

Council of the EU · draft ST 14872/26
10OCT 2026Technical readinessGrade BMinister describes six remaining actions

Event: 10 October 2026

In a RIK interview, Nicolas Ioannides named early November as the expected completion date. The minister also expected accession in 2027. The six actions in the interview and the six areas in the registered draft refer to different things.

Why it matters

The statement clarifies the government's plans. Actual completion needs separate confirmation.

RIK · Ioannides interview
07OCT 2026PoliticsGrade BMediterranean EU countries support Cyprus's progress

Event: 7 October 2026

In a joint declaration, the nine MED9 countries welcomed the positive report and the start of Council discussions. Adopted in Split on 7 October, the declaration called for timely completion of the remaining stages.

Why it matters

Support from several countries improves the prospect of agreement. A decision requires unanimity.

MED9 group · Split declaration Full MED9 declaration
05OCT 2026ProcedureGrade ACouncil registers report on action-plan implementation

Event: 5 October 2026

The register published a record for ST 13957/26. The document's title and number were registered on 5 October. The full report is not public.

Why it matters

A document title is insufficient to assess implementation of individual recommendations.

Council of the EU · register ST 13957/26
01OCT 2026PoliticsGrade BCyprus announces implementation of recommendations

Event: 1 October 2026

Ioannides said Cyprus was ready to move to political agreement. He spoke on 1 October; the government announcement was published on 2 October.

Why it matters

The Cypriot government's position clarifies preparation progress. Completion of the procedure depends on the Council of the EU.

Cyprus government · Ioannides statement
15SEP 2026ProcedureGrade ACountry report reaches the working party

Event: 15 September 2026

EU Council meeting papers include the Schengen report on Cyprus. It is listed among the Schengen working party documents for 15 September.

Why it matters

The dossier has moved to Council discussion.

Council of the EU · working party papers of 15 September
14JUL 2026Technical readinessGrade A / BCommission gives a positive assessment of technical preparations

Event: 14 July 2026

The committee delivered a positive opinion on 26 June. The country report was adopted on 14 July. The Commission outlined the evaluation at its 15 July briefing.

Why it matters

A positive technical assessment allows progress towards a political decision.

European Commission · briefing of 15 July
21MAY 2026PoliticsGrade BCyprus president outlines timing of a political decision

Event: 21 May 2026

The president expected a political decision in late 2026 or early 2027. This assessment was given in an official statement on 21 May.

Why it matters

The statement reflects Nicosia's expectations at the time.

President of Cyprus · statement of 21 May
25APR 2023Technical readinessGrade ACouncil of the EU authorises SIS application in Cyprus

Event: 25 April 2023

Decision 2023/870 extended the Schengen Information System provisions to Cyprus. It was adopted on 25 April. Cyprus began applying the SIS provisions on 25 July 2023.

Why it matters

Information-sharing was a practical step towards integration. Border checks remain in place.

EUR-Lex · Council Decision (EU) 2023/870 Cyprus Interior Ministry · SIS connection
